overview.short: Thirunadhikkara Cave Temple is an ancient 7th-to-8th century rock-cut cave shrine in Thirunanthikarai, Kanyakumari district, Tamil Nadu. Perched by the Kodayar river, it features monolithic pillars, ancient lingam sanctum, and historic rock inscriptions of Chola King Rajaraja I.
overview.description: Thirunandikkara Cave Temple, also referred to as Thirunanthikarai rock-cut Shiva temple, is a 9th-century rock-cut Hindu cave temple in Kanyakumari district, Tamil Nadu, India. It is dedicated to Shiva, with murals and inscriptions. It is attributed to the Ay king Vikramaditya Varaguna by Archaeological Survey of India, but to Pandya rulers (Nedunjadaiyan) a few decades earlier by Ajit Kumar, an archaeologist.
